citations.review_text: One of the best multiplayer FPS games out there. The graphics and gameplay hold up well too and the campaign is good too. People also still play this game too. You also don’t need a client either like the older COD games. The only downside to this game is that it can take forever to get into a match and the menu can glitch out but other than that it’s a solid game.

I quite enjoy playing this game again, used to play it on my PS4 years ago when I didn't have my laptop. Runs very well, and still is pretty fun to play. I play on European servers, and sometimes it takes 5-10 minutes to find games, other times it's 1-2 minutes, which is understandable as this isn't the newest game. Be that as it may, definitely worth the buy, especially when it's discounted to a couple euros. One of the few EA games that are actually playable without shoving microtransactions down your throat.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe movement mechanics that include sliding, wall-running, and double-jumping.

citations.review_text:
Played it for the first time in 2026 and it still holds up perfectly fine after 10 years, both visually and mechanically. The campaign is short, fast-paced and tons of fun. On-foot gameplay feels great with all the sliding, wall running and double jumping you can do while shooting, and the Titan sections give you access to a bunch of different mecha weapons that all have their own unique play styles. My only complaint is that some of the locations felt a little bland at times; the game starts strong with its lush jungle setting, but then some of the later missions just take place inside boring, gray, metallic buildings and facilities.

Overall though, if you like giant robots and first-person shooters, this game's a no-brainer. Trust me.

Titanfall 2 proves that a tightly packed 6-hour campaign will always beat a 50-hour bloated open world.

Pros:
Wall-running, double-jumping, slide-hopping. Momentum preservation is king here - it scratches the exact same itch as Ghostrunner, just with firearms.
The game never runs out of ideas — just look at the time-travel device.
The deadpan dynamic and buddy-cop chemistry between the pilot and BT genuinely works without feeling cheesy.
Mech combat: Fighting inside the cockpit shifts the pace into heavy, tactile warfare. The campaign constantly feeds you brand-new Titan loadouts on the fly to keep encounters fresh.
No side quests, no map markers, no wasted minutes. You hit start and the game maintains high velocity until the credits roll.

Cons:
Ends too quickly.

single_points.text: One reviewer says they got caught in a complex wall climb that took far too long to randomly pass and that one boss fight seemed impossible.

citation.review_text: It is a great game but I gave it a thumbs down because of some of the mechanics.  I got caught in complex wall climb that took far too long to randomly pass.  And one boss fight seemed impossible.  Yes, I got through, but running into those tough spots really took the fun out of it.  Maybe after dying a 100 times the devs could ask if I need help skipping the section instead of giving up for a day or two after getting stuck.

citations.review_text: Best FPS I've ever played and the campaign is addictive, but EA is scummy with their launcher. Great game tho :)

Titanfall 2 is a highlight of the FPS genre. The single player campaign is great, and the PvP is one of the few instances of FPS PvP that I actually have fun with. The Frontier Defense gamemode (wave-based 4-player PvE) is my absolute favorite part; I reached max upgrades with every titan. The single player campaign is relatively short, but uses that time to constantly explore unique mechanics and environments, without giving you the time to get bored. Even on the highest difficulty, the campaign tends to be on the easier side, but it never really bothered me. This game also has earned it's place as one of the defining games of the movement shooter genre: every piece of the movement system feels fluid and can cleanly join into the next movement.

The biggest negative to the game is that you have to engage with the EA launcher and the problems associated with that. I regularly had issues connecting to multiplayer anything or lobbies with my friends.

I beat the single player campaign in ~8 hours, then an additional ~3 hour to 100% achievements.

This game is one of the Top 3 human inventions of all time, and you NEED to try the SMR Primary with Amped Boost or A-Wall Pilot; it shreds through Titans like butter.

I’ve beaten the campaign like 5 times, I wouldn’t say it’s the best campaign or anything but it’s definitely worth trying.

The multiplayer is like the main reason to get the game, that’s where all the real fun is, getting called slurs in chat and hackers spamming links to their Discord servers so you can buy their hacks.

 The pilot weapons are ok but we all know the SMR is the best weapon hands down.

You’ll unfortunately, need the EA app downloaded to play this.
(Suck a fat one EA)

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the single-player campaign as short in length.

citations.review_text:
So many good things I could say about this game. The single player campaign is amazing with all levels being great, BT is an amazing and surprisingly deep character, and the only bad thing to say is that it's too short.

The multiplayer is fun, fast, the movement can be crazy but also hard for newcomers to get into, especially now.

And speaking of the movement, it's not really difficult to start out with it, but there is a bunch of tech you can master. But even just slide hopping and wall running feels great and is so much fun.


Even just for the campaign alone, this game is worth it.
Best story I have every played. Short, 6-ish hours, and yet the most interesting and rewarding story.

Titanfall 2 is a peak game and one of the best shooters to play. The campaign is a genuinely great story, the only problem with is is that it is only 4-6 hours long which leaves content to be desired. The multiplayer scene is small but is satisfying and rewarding once you get past the steep learning curve. This game is highly recommended if it is 85-90% off, unless you want to give more money than you should to EA.

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the multiplayer has a steep learning curve and features long-time players, making it difficult for newcomers.

citations.review_text:
[h1][b]The[/b] movement shooter[/h1]
No really its soo good. The movement system, the rock-paper-scissors with the giant mechs, the way those 2 completely different games coexist in the same place at the same time and even interact, the frantic magdump when you are trying to swat that annoying pilot flying around as the mech or the dodging bullets that you know will kill you in 1 hit but you still jump there,... 
[hr][/hr]
I love the combat and game mechanics. Titan vs titan feels like playing chess but fast with your life on the line, pilot vs pilot is really fast paced and puts emphasis on the third dimension and titan vs pilot feels like a bossfight balanced so that no matter which side you are on you will barely win. 
Oh and [i]the finishers[/i]!  And unique abilities for both titans and pilots... 
[hr][/hr]
The only problem with the game is that its so old. The graphics are still VERy good and the servers run great, but 99% of the playerbase has played the game for over 6 years and the skill ceiling is really high and it wont be easy for newcomers. [b]Seriously play the campaign first if you want to get a single kill in pvp. I havent seen a more fun and usefull tutorial. Ever. [/b] It will teach you all the major / intended game mechanics and force you to gain the skills required to evolve past sitting ducks on the battlefield. Gl and GG

Titanfall 2 is a peak game and one of the best shooters to play. The campaign is a genuinely great story, the only problem with is is that it is only 4-6 hours long which leaves content to be desired. The multiplayer scene is small but is satisfying and rewarding once you get past the steep learning curve. This game is highly recommended if it is 85-90% off, unless you want to give more money than you should to EA.

It's 2026 and I'm reinstalling the game again. I take breaks from time to time, but this one is like Minecraft for me: I'll always come back to it. After all the new releases we've gotten over the years, this one still holds its place as my favorite video game of all time.

I really enjoyed the campaign for this game, and I wish it didn't come to an end as soon as it did. When I first started playing this game, I wasn't too interested in playing PvP (in any game). I spent many hours in frontier defense, and I enjoyed it the entire time. Eventually I did get bored of it, so I tried my hand at some of the PvP modes. The variety that provided kept me in the game for years to come.

I'm now rotating this game back in after a few years break, so I'm bound to be rusty. If you're a new player trying to get into it, just be aware that everyone else has been playing for a while. It takes some time to learn the movement, don't get discouraged. I'll be right there along with you after my time away.

⭐️/10
